profile_summary: Technical product manager out of regulated money movement. At Bank of China I ran e-banking and BOC Pay delivery where compliance set the launch gate: 100% of HKMA mandates cleared inside a hard 14-day window, Geo-IP fraud detection shipped against it, and a 3-year incident-triage backlog closed by specifying an anomaly-detection prototype with a developer. That is where I learned where a model earns its place and where a deterministic check has to hold. No neobank or Southeast Asia superapp on the record, the honest match is that regulated-delivery record: correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners nobody controls.

bullets: Cut USD 2 per unit in product cost for a Tier-1 UK mobile network operator by making the case across GTM roadmap and pricing reviews that a feature carried no weight in the customer's buying decision, then removing it from the device configuration.
Validated solution feasibility across 6 account subnets before proposal commitment, as dedicated presales cover inside a 5-person pursuit team.

Cut the manual layer out of a 60 to 80 unit evaluation programme with VBA automation and a scheduled task, replacing a daily hand-check of every live sample with automated deadline reminders and cutting about an hour a week of sign-off document assembly.

Cleared 100% of HKMA regulatory mandates inside a hard 14-day window, shipping Geo-IP fraud detection with impossible-travel logic, by turning the regulation into an implementation plan and running internal teams alongside third-party vendors against the gate.

Closed a 3-year backlog in e-banking incident triage by specifying and validating a Python anomaly-detection prototype, built with a developer, that separated critical incidents from deployment noise across 50,000+ historical logs.
Kept competing projects moving by arbitrating manday conflicts across priorities, either absorbing dependent work directly or building the business case for a timeline change.

Standardised requirements intake on a 7-question elicitation framework covering objective, context, stakeholders, success criteria, scope, constraints and evidence sources, closing gaps through follow-up interviews before anything reached JIRA.
Recovered 8 hours a week of manual reporting effort across 20 systems, roughly 400 hours a year, by deploying a centralised Grafana observability framework in place of hand-assembled weekly reports.
Defused rollback demands in the middle of a POS migration by showing store leaders the original report flow still ran as a fallback and committing technical support through the transition.
Reversed a headquarters decision by presenting evidence that store operations varied by location, moving the Shanghai development team off centralised training onto store-specific delivery.

Generated GBP 350,000 in new B2B pipeline across a 50+ account portfolio by running discovery, solution positioning and qualification end to end, then escalating matured accounts to the corporate sales team to close.
